note: Office workers, lunch crowds, buyers, trade-dinner guests (Fifth Ave, Herald Sq, Madison Sq).

lines.text: Morning. Excuse me. Morning.
Hot enough for you? Ha. Everybody says that.
Forty-five minutes for lunch. I eat in twelve and stare for thirty-three.
They're talking layoffs on the eighth floor. Again.
Bought a calculator. Electric. Fits in my pocket. Ninety dollars!
Insurance. We insure everything except the city.
City can't pay its bills. I can't pay mine. Solidarity.
Subway stalled twenty minutes under Thirty-Fourth. In the dark.
Fare's thirty-five cents and the car smells like a gym.
My boss wants me in at eight. The train wants me in at nine.
Rain, and I left my umbrella at the office. Which is where I am.
Taxi! Taxi! Nobody stops for a man in rain.
Office air-conditioning broke. We're working in our socks.
Tie in August. The things we do for pensions.
Honking won't move Fifth Avenue, friend.
Green light! It's green! Go!
Excuse me! Watch where you're going!
Sorry. Sorry. My fault. No, your fault. Sorry.
Whoa! Late for a meeting?
Running in a suit? Somebody's in trouble.
Hey! That's a sidewalk! For walking!
Elevator's stuck between floors. With my boss in it. Hmm.
Power's out. Guess we're closing early. Shame.
Working late. The building sighs at night. You hear it?
Lunch at the counter. Tuna on rye. Same as every day.
Did you see the Empire State lit up last night? Beautiful.
My cousin's moving to Jersey. Says the city's finished.
Good afternoon. Lovely day for a deal.
Phone company says two weeks for a new line. Two weeks!
Garment buyers in town. Every restaurant smells like cologne.
Share the awning? Plenty of room.
